issue_context.title: Fix broadcasting for `repeat_by`
issue_context.body:
### Problem description

The result of
```
pl.int_ranges(0, 3)
```
can be achieved by 
```
pl.int_range(0, 3).implode()
```

There is also pl.repeat, which doesn't have any pl.repeat**s**

Maybe I am missing something (performance, ...), but it makes no sense in this case.
comments: `int_ranges` allows for specifying expression based ranges i.e. ranges that depend on start and end points of different columns or expressions on those columns. You can therefore have a _different_ length of and contents of lists per row, which isn't possible with `int_range`.

I had a similar use-case recently, wanting to copy/clone the shapes/structure of an existing list column.

<strike>The closest I got was `pl.when()` inside `.list.eval`</strike>

```python
df.with_columns(
   pl.int_ranges(0, "n").list.eval(pl.when(pl.element() == pl.element()).then(0))
)

# The predicate '[(col("")) == (col(""))]' in 'when->then->otherwise' is not a valid aggregation and might produce a different number of rows than the group_by operation would. This behavior is experimental and may be subject to change
# shape: (3, 3)
# ┌───────┬─────┬───────────┐
# │ start ┆ n   ┆ int_range │
# │ ---   ┆ --- ┆ ---       │
# │ i64   ┆ i64 ┆ list[i32] │
# ╞═══════╪═════╪═══════════╡
# │ 0     ┆ 1   ┆ [0]       │
# │ 0     ┆ 2   ┆ [0, 0]    │
# │ 0     ┆ 3   ┆ [0, 0, 0] │
# └───────┴─────┴───────────┘
```
**Update:** Forgot about [`.repeat_by`](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/10702#issuecomment-1692853188) - thanks @reswqa
Makes sense - we should be able to add this.

@stinodego I'm a bit confused, how different is this from `repeat_by`?

```python
    df = pl.DataFrame({
        "start": [0,0,0]
        ,"n": [1,2,3]
    })

    df = df.with_columns([
        pl.col("start").repeat_by(pl.col("n")).alias("repeat")
    ])

```

```python
┌───────┬─────┬───────────┐
│ start ┆ n   ┆ repeat    │
│ ---   ┆ --- ┆ ---       │
│ i64   ┆ i64 ┆ list[i64] │
╞═══════╪═════╪═══════════╡
│ 0     ┆ 1   ┆ [0]       │
│ 0     ┆ 2   ┆ [0, 0]    │
│ 0     ┆ 3   ┆ [0, 0, 0] │
└───────┴─────┴───────────┘
```

> how different is this from repeat_by?

You're right, it's not. Forgot we already had that functionality.

> both functions would be just merged

Nope, because the expressions have different return types. This is the reason `int_range/s` have been split into two different functions to begin with.

I think one slight difference is that `.repeat_by` requires the LHS to be the same height e.g. you cannot do:
```python
df = pl.DataFrame({ "A": [[1, 2], [1, 2, 3], [0]] })

# shape: (3, 1)
# ┌───────────┐
# │ A         │
# │ ---       │
# │ list[i64] │
# ╞═══════════╡
# │ [1, 2]    │
# │ [1, 2, 3] │
# │ [0]       │
# └───────────┘

df.with_columns(pl.lit(0).repeat_by(pl.col("A").list.lengths()))

# ComputeError: Length of repeat_by argument needs to be 1 or equal to the length of the Series. 
# Series length 1, by length 3
```
But we can create a column first:
```python
df.with_columns(zero = 0).with_columns(pl.col("zero").repeat_by(pl.col("A").list.lengths()))

# shape: (3, 2)
# ┌───────────┬───────────┐
# │ A         ┆ zero      │
# │ ---       ┆ ---       │
# │ list[i64] ┆ list[i32] │
# ╞═══════════╪═══════════╡
# │ [1, 2]    ┆ [0, 0]    │
# │ [1, 2, 3] ┆ [0, 0, 0] │
# │ [0]       ┆ [0]       │
# └───────────┴───────────┘
```
Whereas the suggested enhancement would be:
```python
df.with_columns(
   pl.repeats(0, pl.col("A").list.lengths())
)
```
@cmdlineluser I thinks for this case we should extends `repeat_by` to support broadcasting not only RHS but also LHS. 🤔 It will only broadcast the RHS value now.
@cmdlineluser Good catch - this is a bug. I repurposed this issue. We should fix the broadcasting for `repeat_by`.

review_comments: I believe we can share most of the code with these types, but before that, maybe we should unify this call first. 🤔
Yes, might be a good follow up!
